facts: **$l = r\theta$**, where $r$ is the radius and $\theta$ is the central angle **in radians**.
If the angle is in degrees, convert it first using $\theta = \alpha^{\circ} \times \dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$.
Rearranging gives the radius $r = \dfrac{l}{\theta}$ and the angle $\theta = \dfrac{l}{r}$.
The arc length $l$ is measured in the same units as the radius $r$.
For a full turn $\theta = 2\pi$, so the formula gives the circumference $l = 2\pi r$.
A **minor arc** has $\theta < \pi$, and a **major arc** has $\theta > \pi$.
steps: Ensure the central angle $\theta$ is in radians, converting from degrees if required.
Write the arc length formula $l = r\theta$.
Substitute the known values (or rearrange to solve for $r$ or $\theta$).
Evaluate the expression and state the result in exact form with $\pi$ or rounded as specified.

foundation.question_text: A circle has a radius of $6\text{ cm}$. Find the exact length of an arc that subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
Find the length of an arc in a circle of radius $15\text{ cm}$ that subtends a central angle of $1.4\text{ radians}$.
A circle has a radius of $12\text{ cm}$. Find the exact length of an arc that subtends an angle of $60^{\circ}$ at the centre.
An arc of length $10\pi\text{ cm}$ subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$. Find the radius of the circle.
In a circle of radius $8\text{ cm}$, an arc has length $12\text{ cm}$. Find the central angle $\theta$ in radians.
A circle has a radius of $5\text{ cm}$. A minor arc subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$ at the centre. Find the exact length of the major arc.
A pendulum of length $45\text{ cm}$ swings through an angle of $0.4\text{ radians}$. Find the distance travelled by the tip of the pendulum bob.

development.question_text: A circle has a radius of $14\text{ m}$. Find the length of an arc subtending an angle of $135^{\circ}$ at the centre, correct to two decimal places.
An arc of length $7.5\text{ cm}$ subtends a central angle of $1.25\text{ radians}$. Find the radius of the circle.

An arc of length $\dfrac{10\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$ in a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ subtends a central angle $\theta$. Find the exact value of $\theta$ in radians, and state its equivalent size in degrees.
A minor arc subtends an angle of $50^{\circ}$ at the centre of a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$. Calculate the exact length of the corresponding major arc.

mastery.question_text: A satellite orbits Earth at an orbital radius of $7000\text{ km}$. It travels along its circular path at a speed of $7.5\text{ km/s}$ for $20\text{ minutes}$. Find the central angle subtended in radians, correct to three decimal places.
In a circle of radius $r$, an arc of length $l = \dfrac{8\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ where $0 < \theta \leq \dfrac{4\pi}{5}$. Find the minimum possible value of the radius $r$.
Two points $P$ and $Q$ on a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ divide the circumference in the ratio $3:5$. Find the exact length of the major arc $PQ$.
mastery.solution_text:
The major arc subtends $\dfrac{5}{3+5} = \dfrac{5}{8}$ of a full turn:
$\theta_{\text{major}} = \dfrac{5}{8} \times 2\pi = \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$
$l = r\theta$
$= 6 \times \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$
$= \dfrac{15\pi}{2}\text{ cm}$
